function.mechanism: Hydrates to form viscous colloidal systems and films that increase viscosity and stabilize dispersed phases.

adi.basis: EFSA ANS Panel (2018) concluded there is no need for a numerical ADI for celluloses including E464.

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern for reported uses and exposure; no numerical ADI needed, with specification-related contaminant caveats.

adi.basis: JECFA records indicate ADI not specified/not limited for hydroxypropyl methyl cellulose in early evaluations.

concerns.summary: Recent review literature raises mechanistic concern that some cellulose-based food thickeners may affect gut microbiota and related physiology, but direct high-quality causal harm evidence specific to E464 remains limited.
Regulatory concern focuses on material specifications (possible toxic element and microbiological impurity limits), not intrinsic toxicity at authorized use levels.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2018 found no safety concern at reported uses/exposure and no need for a numerical ADI.
Longstanding FDA authorization under 21 CFR 172.874 with GMP-based conditions of use.
No IARC monograph classification identified for hydroxypropyl methyl cellulose.

populations: children (highest estimated exposure on a bodyweight basis)
infants and toddlers (elevated bodyweight-normalized intake compared with adults)
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA/JECFA did not set a numerical ADI for E464; EFSA high-percentile exposure estimates in children were not interpreted as indicating a safety concern.

risk_assessment.rationale: Evidence from EFSA/JECFA/FDA supports continued approval with no strong direct hazard signal for normal food uses; residual uncertainty is mainly specification quality control and indirect microbiome hypotheses rather than robust demonstrated harm for E464.
key_factors: EFSA 2018: no numerical ADI needed; no safety concern at reported uses/exposure
FDA listing as permitted direct food additive under 21 CFR 172.874 with GMP conditions
JECFA historical ADI not specified/not limited with older data-gap caveat for some high-substitution products
Recent mechanistic concern literature exists but is indirect/low-specificity for E464
